title: Spatial atlas of the human brain vasculature reveals specialized cell ensembles.
journal: Cell 189(19), Sep 2026 (PMID 42537647). NIHMS author manuscript PMC13577656, read via NCBI efetch. Europe PMC lists isOpenAccess=N, license 'cc by'; its fullTextXML endpoint returned HTTP 500.
data_url: GEO GSE335898 (BioProject PRJNA1479806; 15 GSMs; GSE335898_RAW.tar 158 GB) ; UCSC Cell Browser https://cells.ucsc.edu/?ds=brain-vasc-spatial (cell-human, cell-mouse, spatial-ctx, spatial-hc) ; code https://github.com/jwangbio/spatial-brain-vasc (3 R scripts, no licence)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: GEO: read filelist.txt (15 GSMs = 4 cortex slides + 11 hippocampus sections; per-GSM morphology.ome.tif 2.5-19.5 GB, transcripts.parquet 68 MB-2.2 GB, cell_feature_matrix.h5 0.8-13 MB, cells.parquet 0.27-3.8 MB). Downloaded 2 h5 files: raw int32 counts, 300 genes with Ensembl IDs plus 241 control codewords; 33,445 and 197,723 onboard-segmented cells. Of the 26,088 labelled cell-browser cells in section 0079638_1, 0 match the GEO barcodes. Cell browser: downloaded human/mouse/hippocampus meta.tsv (28/15/23 MB) and both Spatial.coords files. Range-read the cortex meta header (93 MB file) and the first 3 MB of hc exprMatrix: dense genes x 373,794 cells, normalized non-integer values. Decoded the per-field binary metadata to crosstab every cortex cell. Every count matched the paper exactly: 314,535 / 206,654 / 1,155,946 / 373,794 cells; 101,929 and 52,739 vascular cells; 57,826 cortical ECs; 6 donors/9 sections in cortex, 7/11 in hippocampus, 39 donors/5 studies in scRNA. No duplicate Cell_IDs or NAs.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: How Subtype_ID and Domain_ID were made: scVI/scANVI plus Leiden plus manual top-25-marker naming for scRNA; Baysor segmentation, BANKSY lambda=0.2/0.95 and Slingshot/Monocle3 cut points for spatial. Also epilepsy-resection vs postmortem tissue source and the MAGMA/Drug2Cell results. Tables S1-S7 were not retrieved: PMC serves a proof-of-work page, and the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint says 'not open access'. The Seurat RDS files (142 MB-2.4 GB) and the 1.67-1.83 GB scRNA count mtx files exceed the 50 MB cap and were not opened. The coordinate unit is assumed to be um; the files do not state it.

a1_downloadable.note: Pass (checked). GEO per-sample files and every cell-browser file return HTTP 200 anonymously. Only the supplementary xlsx tables were unreachable, and they are not needed for any task.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Mechanical pass (checked). Subtype_ID is a column (27 human scRNA / 21 mouse / 33 cortex / 34 hippocampus classes), and so is Domain_ID (9 cortical laminae/WM/LM classes; 10 hippocampal subfield classes). Both are author annotations, not measurements; see A8.

a3_inputs_present.note: Pass with a cost (checked). The labelled spatial expression is a dense genes x cells normalized TSV (hc 90 MB gz, ctx 162 MB gz, 300 genes); x/y coordinates come in a separate file. Raw counts for the labelled Baysor cells are not in GEO (0/26,088 barcode overlap), so only normalized values or the RDS are usable.

a4_units_stated.note: Weak pass. Labels are categorical. Expression is volume-normalized and then SCT-transformed (per the paper; the file only shows floats). The coordinate unit is unstated, and the cortex x range of 113-43,249 exceeds one Xenium slide, so per-section offsets are likely (inferred).

a5_enough_rows.note: Fail in disguise. There are 154,668 labelled spatial vascular cells and 167,573 scRNA vascular cells, but those labels fail A8. For the physically measured labels (donor, age, sex, preservation, region) the unit is the donor: 13 spatial donors (6 cortex, 7 hippocampus) and 39 scRNA donors in 5 studies, all checked. Region_ID outside cortex/hippocampus is 100% Siletti.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Spatial: about 1.4 GB dense float32 (cortex 1.16M x 300) plus 0.45 GB (hippocampus), or under 0.2 GB for vascular cells only. scRNA human: 1.83 GB mtx.gz, likely several GB sparse in memory (not opened).
a6_fits_laptop.note: Passes for the spatial vascular subset on CPU. The scRNA side and the GEO images/transcripts (TB-scale tar) do not fit comfortably.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Pass (checked): every cell, vascular, donor and section count matches the paper exactly. Oddities: two cortex Donor_ID values are '<1' and '40', which look like age strings rather than IDs, though each still maps 1:1 to sections. The hippocampus meta lacks Sex_ID.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL. Subtype_ID comes from Leiden clustering on scVI/scANVI embeddings (scRNA) or BANKSY embeddings (spatial, lambda=0.2, which mixes in neighbour expression) of the same expression, named by Wilcoxon markers. Domain_ID is BANKSY lambda=0.95 plus trajectory cut points built from expression and coordinates. Predicting either from expression reproduces the authors' clustering, which is leakage by construction. The labels are also study-confounded: Matrix_PC is 18,865/19,057 Yang, and Arterial_SMC is 16,807/19,134 Winkler (checked).

existing_models.name: STAMapper (Genome Biology 2025, 10.1186/s13059-025-03773-6, PMC12502291)
existing_models.score_and_split: Heterogeneous GNN for scRNA-to-single-cell-spatial label transfer. Best accuracy on 75 of 81 scST datasets across 8 technologies, against scANVI, RCTD and Tangram. On one Xenium colon dataset the search summary gives 93.91% vs RCTD 92.23%, scANVI 66.33% and Tangram 37.89% (that number not verified in full text).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: It uses only one scRNA-seq reference, so cell types missing from that reference are lost. They suggest multiple references as future work.

existing_models.name: Xenium annotation benchmark: SingleR/Azimuth/RCTD/scPred/scmapCell (BMC Bioinformatics 2025, PMC11744978)
existing_models.score_and_split: Single human breast cancer Xenium dataset, compared against manual marker annotation. SingleR ranked best; no held-out-donor split.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Reference quality dominates, and snRNA references are preferable for imaging platforms.

existing_models.name: Nicheformer (Nature Methods 2025, PMC12695652; github theislab/nicheformer, BSD-3; weights on Mendeley Data)
existing_models.score_and_split: Spatial foundation model (110M cells). Highest macro F1 for linear-probe cell-type/niche/region label prediction on MERFISH mouse brain, ahead of Geneformer, scGPT, UCE and CellPLM. PCA with many components was 'practically on par' with a linear probe.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Tissues with low abundance in SpatialCorpus underperform scVI/PCA unless pretraining is extended. Dropping contextual tokens may discard information.

backbone.name: Nicheformer (spatial and dissociated cells; frozen linear probe). Geneformer/scGPT would fit only the full-transcriptome scRNA side, and a 300-gene panel is a poor fit for rank-based tokenization.
backbone.hardware: CPU for embedding the about 155k spatial vascular cells (hours; not timed). Full 1.5M cells or the scRNA counts would want a GPU or a long run.
backbone.licence: Nicheformer code BSD-3; Mendeley weights licence not checked. Cell-browser data has no stated licence, and the article is labelled cc by in Europe PMC.

integration.partner_dataset: Not scored (stopped at A8). The natural partner is SEA-AD / Allen MTG MERFISH (same middle temporal gyrus, different platform).
integration.join_key: Gene symbol (Ensembl IDs are in the GEO h5) plus harmonized cell-class label. The join is at label level, not row level.

controls.positive_control: Not assessed. The paper's own controls are the marker genes MGP/MFSD2A/ACKR1 along the arteriovenous axis and the myeloid-MS MAGMA association.
controls.negative_control: Not assessed (the paper uses ambidexterity GWAS as a null trait).
controls.external_validation: Not assessed. The human vs mouse atlas (206,654 cells) and cortex vs hippocampus would be the second sources, but all their labels share the same annotation provenance.

honest_claim_h3: At best: 'a classifier reproduces these authors' vascular-subtype clustering of 300-gene Xenium cells from 13 donors (mostly epilepsy resections), at X% held-out-donor accuracy'. That is a statement about annotation consistency, not vascular biology.
ml_idea: Transfer vascular subtypes and arteriovenous segment from the 314k-cell scRNA atlas to Xenium cells with frozen Nicheformer embeddings plus a linear head, held out by donor or study. This is rejected because both label sets are the same group's clustering output (A8), the study confound is severe, and scRNA-to-Xenium transfer is already benchmarked by STAMapper, SingleR/RCTD and Nicheformer.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already done: tracing Subtype_ID/Domain_ID to clustering of the same expression (A8), and the Subtype_ID x Author_ID crosstab (Matrix_PC 99% Yang). If revived, run leave-Yang-out SingleR on matrix vs transport pericytes; if F1 collapses, the label is a study artefact.

verdict_reason: The data is open, and every count matches the paper exactly. But the only high-n labels (Subtype_ID, Domain_ID) are the authors' clustering of the same expression (A8), and the physically measured labels have just 13 spatial and 39 scRNA donors (A5). B/C/D (8/6/4) are indicative only, scored after the A8 fail; G-J are not scored and ROI is null.
